question: Which of the following books was written by Banabhatta?
solution:
The correct answer is__** Harshacharita.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Harshacharita is the** biography of the Indian emperor Harshavardhana**, who ruled North India from **606 to 647 CE** and was a ruler of the Vardhana dynasty.
 
• It was written by** Banabhatta**, who was a Sanskrit writer in the seventh century CE and was the **Court Poet (Asthana Kavi**) of Harshavardhana.
 
• It was the first composition of Banabhatta and marks the beginning of the writing of historical poetic works in the** Sanskrit language**.
 
• It was written in poetic prose which narrates the **biography of the emperor Harsha in eight chapters.**
 
• It was translated into** English by Edward Byles Cowell and Frederic William Thomas in 1897**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ashtadhyayi.**

 
 
• It means **“Eight Chapters**.
 
• It was written by **Panini.**
 
• It is a treatise on **Sanskrit gramma**r.​
 
 
 
• **​Akbarnama**.
 
 
• The Akbar Nama is the official chronicle of the **reign of Akbar**.
 
• It was written by his court historian and biographer,** Abu'l-Fazl ibn Mubarak**.
 
• He was one of the **"nine jewels in Akbar's cour**t".
 
• It was written in **Persian**.​
 
 
 
• **Malavikagnimitram**.
 
 
• ​It is written by Kalidas.
 
• The Mālavikāgnimitram is a Sanskrit play by Kālidāsa, based on some events of the reign of Pushyamitra Shunga.
